# File servers

_nextop 0.1.3_

One folder per file server: `file_servers/<name>/file_server.json` (definition only; files live in each run).
Reserved file server names: `knowledge`.

Anyone on a share line uploads files and owns them. When an owner's block ends, its files are shared with the
receivers of its share line, and each receiver becomes an owner too (it can share them on). There is no built-in
search or generation: tools and functions make files, workers and functions upload them.

```json
{
  "name": "materials",
  "description": "pictures, charts and notes made for the video",
  "map_llm": "<model name>",
  "index": "lightrag",
  "shares": [
    { "from": "intake",  "to": ["explainer"] },
    { "from": "photo",   "to": ["planner"] },
    { "from": "planner", "to": ["designer", "editor"] }
  ]
}
```

## file_server.json

| field | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | folder name | file server name: lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits, underscores |
| `description` | "" | read by the LLM in tool descriptions; make it specific; no two file servers may share it |
| `llm` | "default" | LLM adapter that builds the maps of text files |
| `map_llm` | none | model that builds the maps of text files (.md, .txt); without it a map is the first sentences |
| `index` | none | entry name in adapters.index; text files go in; everyone on a share line then gets the query tool |
| `shares` | [] | share lines: who shares with whom (below) |

## Share line

| field | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | required | the sender: a worker id, or a function with FILES_OUT = True |
| `to` | required | the receivers: worker ids or functions with FILES_IN = True (one string or a list) |

- One share line per sender per file server. A receiver waits until its senders' blocks have ended.
- The studio shows the same list as dashed lines on the FLOW canvas and under FILE SERVERS.
- Inside a parallel section copy n shares with copy n (`photo@2` -> `planner@2`); a receiver outside the
  section gets the files of every copy.

## A file

| field | set by | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | automatic | fs://<file_server>/<number>; the same content keeps the same address |
| `format` | automatic | the extension: md, txt, json, png, ... |
| `path` | automatic | where the file is on disk (tools and functions read it there) |
| `title` | uploader | a short label |
| `description` | uploader | what the file is; required (10+ characters) unless it is a text file |
| `source` | uploader | where it came from: a web address, a book and page, or 'made here'; never changes |
| `map` | automatic | text files only: summary and parts (#p1, #p2, ...) |
| `owners` | automatic | the uploader and everyone it was shared with; only owners see and share it |

## Uploading

- Workers that send on a share line get `<file_server>_upload` (items: `file` made in this run, or `name` + `text`; with
  `title`, `source`, `description`), `<file_server>_get` (content of a file they own, by address) and, with an
  index, `<file_server>_query` (answers only from text files they own). Owned files are listed in the input.
- Functions return `_uploads` next to their outputs: `[{"file_server", "file", "title", "description", "source"}]`.
- Files the user gives come in through the start function: take a folder path as an INPUTS field and upload
  the files with `_uploads` (the start function needs `FILES_OUT = True`). A function with `FILES_IN = True` gets
  the files it owns under `files/<file_server>` in its inputs (path included).
- Points on the canvas: left/right are report lines, top/bottom are share lines (bottom sends, top receives).
  Workers have both; a function gets them with `FILES_IN` / `FILES_OUT`.

## Share function (optional)

`file_servers/<name>/share.py` with a function `share(file, report, receivers)` picks which files go to whom.
Without it, every owned file goes to every receiver.

```python
from nextop.file_server import addresses_in

def share(file, report, receivers):
    # file: address, number, format, path, title, description, source, owner
    # report: the owner's outputs (a worker names the files it chose by address)
    named = addresses_in(report).get("materials", set())
    return receivers if file["number"] in named else []
```

## Images

`<file_server>_get` on a picture gives a vision model (mark it in project.json:
`adapters.llm.<name>.options.features` `{"<model>": ["vision"]}`) the image itself, once, in the message after the
tool results; other models get its description. Limits: `image_max_mb` (default 2; bigger images are shrunk when
Pillow is installed: `pip install nextop[images]`) and `images_per_turn` (default 4) in project defaults.
